expectedOutcome: After completing the plan, learners can explain states, choices, transition order, and initialization by problem type and maintain a taxonomy of common DP mistakes.
goal: Build stable skills for defining dynamic-programming states, deriving transition equations, and explaining solutions during review.
notRecommendedFor: There's no array or regression base at all.
I just want to study graphs or tree themes.

phases.focus: Practice the meaning of dp[i], initialization, and rolling arrays with linear sequences.
phases.title: One-Dimensional States and Rolling Optimization

phases.focus: Practice choosing state dimensions for grids, knapsack problems, coins, and subsets.
phases.title: Paths, Knapsack, and Choices

phases.focus: Practice two-dimensional indexes, matching relationships, and string partitioning.
phases.title: Subsequences and String Dynamic Programming

phases.focus: Practice holding/not-holding states, transaction constraints, interval DP, and tree DP extensions.
phases.title: State Machines, Intervals, and Trees

recommendedFor: It's easy to confuse knapsacks, subsequences or stock issues.
summary: Use four weeks to focus on dynamic programming, progressing through one-dimensional states, knapsack and paths, subsequences, state machines, intervals, and trees.
targetAudience: Learners who have practiced basic problems but still struggle to define and transition dynamic-programming states reliably.
title: Dynamic Programming Foundations Plan
